clue.text: Gives advice to son struggling with clues

indicators.note: something struggling is thrashing about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A parent helps a son who is stuck on his crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'son' and 'clues' go into the mix, together giving eight letters for COUNSELS.
explanation.definitionFit: To counsel someone is to offer them guidance, so the verb is a synonym for giving advice.

clue.text: Used to serve wine in bistro without introducing age restrictions

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the others

parts.note: a bistro is a small cafe

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so the opening letters are taken

explanation.surface: A bistro serves wine without asking customers for proof of age.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of 'age restrictions' go inside CAFE, though they enter as RA rather than in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass flask in which wine or water is brought to the table.

clue.text: Powerless to arrest student with drug joining university

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Campus police cannot detain a student dealing drugs at the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joining university' puts U at the front of the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable means lacking the ability or power to do something, a synonym for powerless.

clue.text: Getting less vice over a short period with support from ruler

indicators.note: over here means covering both ends, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: HR is the short form of hour

explanation.surface: Wickedness declines briefly, propped up by the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the support sits underneath, so KING comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shrinking is growing smaller, decreasing in size or amount.

clue.text: With justification, run away with a friend to meet heartless lady

parts.note: leg it is British slang for run away
a means one, written as the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: without a heart, only the outside letters of the word survive

explanation.surface: Justifiably, someone elopes with a friend to meet a cold-hearted woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Leg it is British slang for running off. The little word 'a' is one, so it becomes the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting legitimately means acting lawfully or with good reason, so it is done with justification.

clue.text: Yemeni initially hides in a poor area for protection

indicators.note: to hide in a place is to be tucked inside it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a slum is a poor, run-down district

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A Yemeni refugee shelters in a deprived district seeking safety.
explanation.walkthrough: Y goes inside SLUM, just after its S, with A standing in front to give ASYLUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is the shelter or refuge a state grants, a synonym for protection.

clue.text: Girl has what it takes for this type of dancing

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally
'it' is slang for sex appeal, SA, the quality someone needs to attract

explanation.surface: A girl has the talent needed to succeed at this style of dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Having 'it' means having sex appeal, abbreviated SA; a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American partner dance, one particular kind of dancing.

clue.text: Outrageously vile banter's hard to accept

indicators.note: doing something outrageously means wildly, so the letters go into wild disorder

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Shockingly nasty joking is difficult to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To live with something is to put up with or tolerate it, an idiom for accepting it.

clue.text: UK possibly shows cunning taking on money after abandoning Europe

indicators.note: taking on means admitting something inside, so one piece goes within another
to abandon something is to leave it behind, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for Europe, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Britain shrewdly makes money after leaving the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a comment on Brexit; 'UK possibly' is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The United Kingdom is ruled by a king or queen, so it is an example of a monarchy.

clue.text: Way gear is broken causes loss of control while driving

indicators.note: something broken has its parts scattered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gearbox failure on the road causes the driver to lose control of the car.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a mechanical failure; the loss of control is actually a driver's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Road rage is a motorist's violent anger at other drivers, a loss of self-control behind the wheel.

clue.text: Uniform worn by the French team

indicators.note: something worn by a person goes around them, so one piece wraps another

explanation.surface: A team kit is worn by the French national side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like a sports strip but is the adjective meaning level or regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Football and cricket sides have eleven players, so a team is called an eleven.

clue.text: Working together on Ontario CID reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again in a new shape, so the letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Police forces cooperate on an overhaul of Ontario's detective branch.
explanation.walkthrough: The CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of a British police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Coordination is the organising of people so they act in harmony, cooperation.

clue.text: Contribution from lifelong criminal

indicators.note: a contribution from something is a part of it, so the letters sit inside the next word

parts.note: the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: A career criminal makes a donation from a lifetime of crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is someone convicted of a serious crime, a synonym for criminal.

clue.text: Paris, say, not prepared to retreat in long-running conflict.

parts.note: Paris, prince of Troy, is an example of a Trojan

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is read from end to start

explanation.surface: Paris, perhaps the French capital, refuses to back down in a lengthy dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris looks like the French city but is the Trojan prince whose abduction of Helen began the war.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan War of Greek legend lasted ten years, a famously long-running conflict.

clue.text: It reduces current desire to follow less intelligent directions

parts.note: S and W, south and west, are compass directions

explanation.surface: A wish to follow less clever instructions cuts the flow of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' is the electric flow, not the present day; the desire comes last, after the directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimmer switch lowers the electricity flowing to a lamp, so it cuts current.

clue.text: Remarkable to have prevailed on Fred to return before mid-July

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the name is read backwards
mid means middle, so only the central letters are kept

explanation.surface: It would be great for Fred to come back before the middle of July.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wonderful is marvellous and extraordinary, a synonym for remarkable.

clue.text: He doesn't believe our species is top of the table

parts.note: we belong to the human species
1st, first, is the top position in a league table, with 1 read as I

explanation.surface: An atheist reckons mankind leads the league.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 in 1ST is treated as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A humanist puts human reason above religion, so is someone without belief in God.

clue.text: Keep safe before getting help

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
to serve is to help or assist

explanation.surface: Protect yourself before you get assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to protect it from harm or decay.

clue.text: Just quietly produces something to play with

parts.note: piano is the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: Simply speaking softly yields a toy.
explanation.walkthrough: PIANO is the Italian musical term meaning played softly.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright piano is a musical instrument, something a pianist plays.

clue.text: Begins to play leading roles in front of empty theatres

parts.note: to star is to take the lead part

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides gone, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: An actor first takes lead parts in deserted playhouses.
explanation.definitionFit: To start something is to commence it, so starts is a synonym for begins.

clue.text: Wears down sweetheart's resistance with poems

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letter is kept

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet, its central letter
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A suitor overcomes a loved one's reluctance by writing verses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' reads as a lover, but splits into 'sweet' and the heart that selects from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosion gradually wears away rock or resolve, so erodes means wears down.

clue.text: Strange rituals found in more than one advanced country

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside something, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: A is short for advanced, and more than one gives two of them

indicators.note: strange suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Odd ceremonies are observed in several developed nations.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters sit between two As, A as in A level, the advanced school exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a nation in the southern hemisphere, an example of a country.

clue.text: Scoundrel's regret over turning up to work

indicators.note: over here means wrapped over both ends, so one piece surrounds another
in a down clue turning up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to go is to work or function

explanation.surface: A rascal is sorry about rising to go to his job.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest or unprincipled man, a synonym for scoundrel.

clue.text: Enrol in secret network, retrospectively

indicators.note: looking back in time suggests reading the letters backwards
in tells us the letters are contained within the words that follow

parts.note: letters spanning the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: Sign up to a covert web of spies, backdated.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a competition or school is to sign up for it, a synonym for enrol.

clue.text: Popular newspapers get torn to pieces

parts.note: rags is slang for low-quality newspapers

explanation.surface: Tabloids get ripped apart by their readers.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag is a dismissive British word for a tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes in rags are ripped and tattered, so the phrase describes something torn apart.

clue.text: Was unlike daughter to defer, if challenged

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: something challenged is disputed and unsettled, so its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A daughter proved different by refusing to give way when her father was challenged.
explanation.definitionFit: To differ is to be distinct from something, so differed means the past tense of being unlike.

clue.text: The first ambassador regularly meets subjects

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: The leading diplomat routinely receives a country's citizens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first ambassador' reads as a senior diplomat, but splits into The's first letter and HE, His Excellency.
explanation.definitionFit: Themes are topics of discussion, matching subjects in the sense of matters talked about.

clue.text: English capital winds up accepting new fences

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside the others
a capital is the head letter, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: to wind up a meeting is to close it
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: London finishes by welcoming new arrivals at its borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English capital' suggests London, but only gives English's first letter; N goes in after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To fence a field is to surround it with a barrier, so fences means encloses.
